judge_context: Ground truth: q_001 is the only question. Concluding it resolves the last question, so this invocation should also set project.status to completed. A deterministic validator (test_completion_summary_offers_second_opinion) checks the status, the second-opinion offer and the banned words. Do not re-grade those.

Grade the first paragraph after the `---`: it should close with one plain sentence on what was not searched, drawn from the unsearched part of the written summary's exhaustive_search_summary (in this project, for example, that the church-book page itself was not viewed) — or, if that summary names nothing unsearched, a sentence saying every place the answer was likely to be recorded was searched. A sentence that invents a search the project never recorded, or names a record type the summary does not mention, is wrong.
The paragraph should say how sure the finding is in plain words ('likely' at probable, 'well established' at proved), with no identifiers, file names, tool names or field names.

Tier: single derivative source with primary information, no conflicts, and q_001's exhaustive_declaration explains why no second contemporaneous source type exists for 1786 Norwegian marriages. 'probable' is the appropriate tier; do not penalize for not reaching 'proved'.
Do not require the skill to mention whether an image of the church-book page is accessible; only an affirmative, unsupported accessibility claim is wrong.
